title: a selected custom stream outlives its owning child's credential restriction
trigger: It creates real SDK parent and restricted child sessions with prepared-extension rebinding, starts **the parent's ordinary prompt**, waits until the child's selected streaming function enters, disposes the child, then lets the stream complete. `callThroughGate` admits the invocation, but `runOwned` tracks only a thenable return. `AssistantMessageEventStream` is not thenable; its completion is `result()`. The producer can therefore still be working after the owning session has released its credential pool.
how_found_quote: It creates real SDK parent and restricted child sessions with prepared-extension rebinding, starts **the parent's ordinary prompt**, waits until the child's selected streaming function enters, disposes the child, then lets the stream complete

title: a modifier-produced `resolveHeaders` callback escapes the enumerated gates
trigger: The accepted OAuth `modifyModels` callback can return a model carrying the public `Model.resolveHeaders` function. Projection preserves that capability. The actual streaming consumer later executes `resolveHeaders(signal)` without knowing the authoring registration or asking its gate. In both registration phases, a real session is disposed, then the host calls `streamSimple` on a model it cached while live.
how_found_quote: In both registration phases, a real session is disposed, then the host calls `streamSimple` on a model it cached while live

title: top-level configuration getters still run outside admission, including after retirement
trigger: Only the nested `modifyModels` lookup is explicitly admitted at registration. Reads such as `config.streamSimple`, `config.oauth`, `config.fetchDynamicModels`, and other configuration fields remain ordinary property evaluations. The queued probe records a configuration, retires its owner **before draining the existing queue**, then performs the documented host drain. Its `streamSimple` getter runs three times. Real-session controls in both queued and initialized phases call the registration API after disposal.
how_found_quote: The queued probe records a configuration, retires its owner **before draining the existing queue**, then performs the documented host drain. Its `streamSimple` getter runs three times.

title: ModelRegistry withdrawal and source handoff still destroy shared registration state
trigger: Register a parent and live child under the same provider name, then `unregisterProvider(name, childOwner)`. OAuth and usage removal receive the gate, but the custom API is **not unregistered**. Its next lookup still invokes the withdrawn child's stream. At the same time, runtime model overlays and key configuration are deleted for the whole provider, removing the parent's model. Register the same provider name from two different extension sources. Source handoff calls `#clearRuntimeProviderState(providerName)` **without a gate**, clearing the parent's usage registration.
how_found_quote: Register a parent and live child under the same provider name, then `unregisterProvider(name, childOwner)`

title: queued ownership keyed by the configuration object conflates sessions
trigger: A WeakMap from configuration **object** to owner cannot represent two registrations of the same shared object. Queue that same configuration in two runtimes before draining either. The second queue write replaces the first owner. Draining both with the documented three-field queue record registers both as the child; same-gate replacement then collapses them into one entry. After retiring only the child the live parent is no longer selected.
how_found_quote: Queue that same configuration in two runtimes before draining either. The second queue write replaces the first owner.

title: projection and discovery still snapshot methods and lose the author's receiver
trigger: `modifyModels` is captured and later called as `modifier.modify(...)`, where `this` is the registry's `{modify, gate}` record rather than the OAuth object. `fetchDynamicModels` is captured as `fetcher` and called detached. The first two use ordinary class methods reading private fields. The third replaces the author's modifier after registration; a later refresh still invokes the old captured function.
how_found_quote: The first two use ordinary class methods reading private fields. The third replaces the author's modifier after registration; a later refresh still invokes the old captured function.

title: usage request collection still selects before an invalidating await
trigger: `#collectUsageRequests` chooses an entry before calling `#collectProviderRequests`. The latter awaits duplicate pruning and credential/key resolution, then calls `#supports` on the old registration. If the newest session retires during that wait, its gate refuses and the provider contributes no requests. The test starts real `auth.usage.reports()` with a stored credential and parent/child usage registrations, then retires the child while collection is suspended.
how_found_quote: The test starts real `auth.usage.reports()` with a stored credential and parent/child usage registrations, then retires the child while collection is suspended

title: a failed departing usage call installs a cooldown against the live successor
trigger: The selected child's in-flight fetch returns `null` after it has retired or been withdrawn. The failure path selects the parent's failure policy, but still writes a failure cooldown under the shared report key. Even when the refresh epoch requests a successor probe, the recursive read finds that cooldown first and does not call the healthy parent. Both retirement-without-withdrawal and gate-scoped withdrawal reproduce.
how_found_quote: Both retirement-without-withdrawal and gate-scoped withdrawal reproduce

title: the health guard reads a stateful supports getter twice
trigger: `if (provider.supports && !provider.supports(request))` performs a presence read and then another read for the call. A getter that returns a callable on the first read and `undefined` on the next produces a false failed-health result instead of invoking the supported callable.
measured: {"probe":"stateful-supports-getter","reads":2,"fetches":0,"reports":[{"ok":false,"reason":"provider.supports is not a function. (In 'provider.supports(request)', 'provider.supports' is undefined)"}]}
how_found_quote: A getter that returns a callable on the first read and `undefined` on the next produces a false failed-health result instead of invoking the supported callable.
